R012_dayoff.first_comment: Your boss texts on your day off. IGNORE, REPLY or CALL? 👇
R012_dayoff.caption:
Your boss texts on your day off. So what do you actually send back? 👀

"Need you on a call for 5 min."
"I know it's your day off, but..."

Ignore it and you worry all day. Jump on the call and your day off is gone.

There's a third option: one calm line. "I'm off today. I'll handle it first thing tomorrow." Then mute work apps until tomorrow.

And no, it's not just you. Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index found the average worker sends or gets 50+ messages outside core hours.

Silence feels risky.
A call costs your whole day.
One calm line protects both.

That's not lazy. It's how you come back rested.

What do YOU usually do when your boss texts on your day off? 👇

Send this to the always-on coworker.

R013_twojobs.first_comment: Have you ever been handed a coworker's whole job? YES or NO 👇
R013_twojobs.caption:
Your coworker quit. So why is their whole job now YOURS? 👀

Their projects.
Their clients.
Their weekly report.

Same title. Same paycheck. Twice the work.

And it happens a lot: the BLS counted 3.1 million quits in August 2026. Somebody picks up that work.

In healthy workplaces, extra work comes with a plan.
In toxic ones, it just quietly lands on you.

Say: "Happy to help short-term. Which of my projects should pause?" Then put the new priorities in writing the same day.
That's not refusing. It's being realistic.

Have YOU ever been handed someone else's job? 👇

Send this to whoever's doing two jobs.

C006_canceled.first_comment: How many 1:1s has your boss canceled this month? Drop a number 👇
C006_canceled.caption:
Your 1:1 got canceled. Again. What is it really telling you? 👀

"Something came up."
Moved to next week.
Then canceled again.

And you start wondering if you even matter here.

Here's why it's worth fixing: Gallup found managers account for at least 70% of the variance in team engagement. Time with your manager shapes your whole job.

Often it's overload, not dislike.
But the pattern still costs you.

Don't wait quietly to be rescheduled. Ask: "Can we keep 15 minutes Thursday? I need your call on two things." Short and specific is easy to say yes to.
That's not needy. It's doing your job well.

Has YOUR boss canceled on you this month? 👇

Save this for the next cancel, and send it to a coworker who's been skipped.
